verdictRationale: Every executable Phase 5 requirement was independently re-verified with real tests against a real local database and found correct, after fixing one additional real defect this audit itself found (GET /recruitment/applications/:applicationId was still returning unmasked contact fields — missed on the original Phase 5 pass). The five originally NOT EXECUTED tests are confirmed, by code-level audit, to have no corresponding implementation to test — correctly reclassified NOT APPLICABLE, not silently dropped. The remaining BLOCKER is unchanged from the original Phase 5 report and is external to this codebase: no live WhatsApp provider credentials are configured, so WhatsApp message delivery cannot be verified end-to-end with a real provider. This does not affect the authorization/masking logic verified here, which runs the real WhatsApp menu state machine directly.

newDefectFoundThisAudit.finding: GET /recruitment/applications/:applicationId (RecruitmentResumeService.getApplication, used by the website's api.getApplication()) returned the full unmasked candidate object including mobileNumber/email to any recruitment.candidates.review holder, with no recruitment.candidates.contact check at all. This was missed in the original Phase 5 masking pass, which fixed the search/list endpoints but not this one.
newDefectFoundThisAudit.severity: HIGH — same class of defect as the original Phase 5 finding, same violation of 'never rely on hidden UI controls for security.'
newDefectFoundThisAudit.fix: Added an includeContact parameter (default false) to RecruitmentResumeService.getApplication, and the controller now checks recruitment.candidates.contact via AuthorizationService before passing it through — identical pattern to the fix already applied to the search/list endpoints.
newDefectFoundThisAudit.regressionTest: AUDIT-003 (masked) and AUDIT-004 (unmasked when authorized) in recruitment-contact-masking.e2e.spec.ts — both passing.

fiveFormerNotExecutedTests.verificationMethod: Repository-wide grep across apps/api/src/recruitment for "call-status", "call-callback", "providerCallId" (as a write target), and "callback" found zero route/controller/service code that receives or processes any provider call-status event. Additionally, AUDIT-015 directly queries every existing recruitment_call_logs row in the test database and asserts providerCallId and failureReason are null on all of them, confirming no code path populates these columns today.

fiveFormerNotExecutedTests.recommendedNextStep: If automated outbound calling is ever implemented (see the original Phase 5 report's feasibility assessment — currently not feasible: no credentials, no origination code, no consent mechanism), write these five as real tests against the new callback endpoint at that time, reusing the HMAC signature-verification pattern already proven in apps/api/src/voice/voice-webhook.controller.ts and apps/api/src/channels/channel.runtime.ts's verifyTwilioSignature.

exportPolicyFindings.canExportContactFieldsWithoutReviewOrCon: YES — confirmed and verified (AUDIT-010). This is the pre-existing, explicitly documented Sprint 7.16 design decision (see the original code comment in recruitment-export.service.ts: 'mobileNumber/email are still included by default here since the export permission itself already gates all of them'), not an undocumented gap and not something this audit changed.
exportPolicyFindings.tenantAndAuthBoundariesPreservedAcrossPa: YES — the export worker's pagination (RecruitmentExportWorkerService) and status/download endpoints are all organization-scoped at every query; verified in the Sprint 7.17 Phase 3 export-worker test suite (still passing) and re-confirmed here (AUDIT-012: cross-tenant export status/download denied).
exportPolicyFindings.crossTenantExportAccess: DENIED — verified (AUDIT-012): a different organization's token cannot read another organization's export job status or download URL (404 in both cases).
exportPolicyFindings.revokedPermissionCheckedAtExecutionAndDo: Checked at request time (controller guard) and at download time (getDownloadUrl re-validates organizationId + token); NOT re-checked mid-flight for a long-running async export job already queued before revocation — documented as a theoretical, low-severity gap (an export already queued under a since-revoked permission will still complete), not tested further in this pass given the sprint's time constraints.
exportPolicyFindings.csvFormulaInjection: Neutralized — verified against real exported file bytes (AUDIT-013), not just the sanitizer function in isolation.
